On 12 February 2026, a participant was enrolled into the EOPE study with a gestational age incorrectly recorded as 33 weeks at enrollment. Review of source documents subsequently confirmed that the participant’s dating ultrasound performed on 15 January 2026 indicated a gestational age of 16 weeks and 3 days, corresponding to approximately 19 weeks’ gestation at the time of enrollment.
As per the study protocol, eligibility requires a gestational age of ≥23 weeks at enrollment. The participant therefore did not meet the gestational age eligibility criterion, resulting in an eligibility-related protocol deviation.

The deviation has a limited impact on data integrity. Data collected from this participant were obtained following enrollment of an ineligible participant and are therefore not considered per protocol.
The deviation was identified through source verification, documented appropriately, and the correct gestational age was confirmed. Impacted data can be excluded or handled according to the sponsor’s data management and statistical analysis plan, ensuring overall study data integrity is maintained

1.	Reinforcement of protocol requirements regarding gestational age eligibility and source document verification
2.	Implementation of a mandatory pre enrollment eligibility checklist, including confirmation against dating ultrasound reports
3.	Use of obstetric calculators instead of manual calculation
4.	Introduction of additional oversight/verification of gestational age prior to enrollment

The gestational age discrepancy was identified through source document review and verified against the dating ultrasound performed on 15 January 2026. It was confirmed that the participant did not meet the protocol‑specified gestational age eligibility criteria at the time of enrollment.
The protocol deviation was documented and reported in accordance with study, sponsor, and regulatory requirements. The participant voluntarily withdrew from the study on 19 February 2026, and no further study procedures or data collection were performed thereafter.
Corrective and preventive actions were implemented, including reinforcement of gestational age verification against source ultrasound reports prior to enrollment and refresher training of study staff. The deviation has been resolved and closed.

This serious adverse event involves a 32-year-old pregnant participant enrolled in the study on 10 February 2025 who subsequently experienced intrauterine fetal demise (IUFD) at 27+6 weeks gestation. The participant initially met eligibility due to symptoms consistent with suspected preeclampsia (headache and visual disturbances) but was clinically stable at enrolment with no proteinuria and unremarkable systemic findings.
The participant missed her scheduled Visit 2 and became unreachable despite repeated follow-up attempts. On 22 February 2026, she informed the study team that she had been admitted at Parirenyatwa facility on 17 February 2026 following worsening symptoms, including a 3‑day history of headache, lower abdominal pain, flank pain, and absence of fetal movements. Clinical assessment at the facility on admission confirmed intrauterine fetal demise. Laboratory results showed elevated WCC (16.7) with normal haemoglobin (12 g/dL) and platelet count (359). She was admitted and managed for IUFD, undergoing induction of labour with Cytotec, leading to delivery of a macerated stillbirth on 19 February 2026 after 8 hours 55 minutes of labour.
The event meets seriousness criteria due to fetal death and hospitalization and was promptly reported to regulatory authorities per protocol requirements. Causality is unlikely linked to study participation or procedures
Submission of the Serious Adverse Event (SAE) report to the MRCZ and the Sponsor has been completed
